outcome: longer-term mental illness (mental-health related hospitalisation, prescription or death)
cohort: 18,798 women who gave birth between 2008 and 2016 in Grampian, Scotland.
finding: The study found no association between primary postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) and longer-term mental illness beyond the first postnatal year.
mod_finding: The lack of association between PPH and longer-term mental illness was regardless of mode of birth.
